Georgetown teriyaki shop that reopened in early 2026 after a 2023 kitchen fire. Also serves katsu, Mongolian beef and orange chicken.
Interbay teriyaki shop on 15th Ave W, in business since the 1980s. Serves chicken, half chicken and pork teriyaki with cabbage slaw.
Capitol Hill teriyaki counter on E Pike built around teriyaki combinations, plus yakisoba, fried rice and Korean specials.
Bitter Lake teriyaki shop that also does sushi rolls and Chinese wok dishes. Teriyaki plates come with rice and salad.
Teriyaki shop on Rainier Ave S near the I-90 on-ramp, run by owners Yoko and James Wang since 2002. The menu also has tempura, curry, udon, katsudon and oyakodon.
West Seattle Junction teriyaki shop serving chicken and spicy chicken teriyaki, chicken katsu and gyoza.
Teriyaki shop on Rainier Ave S between Mount Baker and Columbia City, serving chicken and beef teriyaki, chicken katsu and gyoza.
Downtown teriyaki counter on Western Ave serving chicken and spicy chicken teriyaki, spicy chicken katsu and gyoza.
Sushi-and-teriyaki shop on Dexter Ave N, with a menu split between teriyaki plates and sushi. Also has poke bowls.
Ballard teriyaki counter on NW Market St with teriyaki plates and combination platters, plus Chinese dishes and noodles.
Georgetown teriyaki shop on 4th Ave S, also serving yakisoba, yaki-udon and Chinese-style dishes such as Mongolian beef.
Greenwood sushi-roll and teriyaki restaurant. Also serves chicken katsu curry, gyoza and poke bowls.
South Lake Union branch of BB's, the build-your-own teriyaki counter. Proteins include spicy chicken, shredded pork, beef brisket and tofu.
Magnolia teriyaki shop on Gilman Ave W serving chicken teriyaki, chicken katsu, yakisoba and gyoza.
Pinehurst teriyaki shop that also serves Chinese dishes and sushi rolls. Teriyaki choices run from chicken and kalbi to salmon and tofu.
Northgate teriyaki shop with teriyaki and teriyaki combos, plus yakisoba, Chinese dishes, bento and kabobs.
Pioneer Square teriyaki counter, also styled Asian Ginger Teriyaki, with teriyaki plates and combos plus stir-fry, yakisoba and fried rice.
Seattle-style teriyaki shop with Hawaiian plate-lunch sides such as Spam musubi and mac salad. One of two Grillbird locations.
SODO shop with a wide menu around its teriyaki section: ramen, sushi rolls, poke bowls and Chinese wok dishes.
Magnolia sushi-and-teriyaki shop, with teriyaki plates and combos as a main menu section next to sushi. Also has kalbi short ribs and donburi.
Teriyaki counter at Seattle Center with halal, gluten-free and vegetarian options. The menu includes teriyaki ribeye, tempura shrimp and crispy tofu.
The second Grillbird location, on Greenwood Ave N. The menu includes chicken teriyaki, katsu, Spam musubi and mac salad.
Ballard teriyaki shop, the first of two Bro's Teriyaki locations. Also serves yakisoba, yakiudon, fried rice and crab rangoon.
Shilshole waterfront seafood house with the Boathouse dining room downstairs and a casual Cafe upstairs. Ray's traces back to a 1939 boat rental and fish-and-chips cafe.
Fish-and-chips stand on Alki Beach, started in 1935 by the Alger brothers in a converted garage on this beachfront. The building has since grown to two stories.

places.n: The Athenian Seafood Restaurant and Bar
places.w: Pike Place Market seafood restaurant and bar, established in 1909. Closed Wednesdays.
Casual oyster bar at Pike Place Market with oyster stew and clam chowder. It sometimes closes for a day to restock after busy weekends.
